mu_name_from: MuMain loads armour indexes 10 to 14 from ArmorElf{i+1} (ZzzOpenData.cpp line 149: `AccessModel(MODEL_ARMOR + i + 10, ..., L"ArmorElf", i + 1)`), so index 13 is ArmorElf04, which openmu's 0.75 Armors.cs names the Spirit Armor. mu.db agrees: code 4109, group 8 index 13, Player/ArmorElf04.bmd.
why_this_one: The Fairy Elf's fourth set and the first of her two that are plate: Eo the Craftsman sells all five pieces at +3 on the first row of his shelf (src/sim/market.cpp, kCraftsman), so Noria's second merchant had a shelf whose top half could not be looked at. Spirit is the Brass set's metal in the elf's green: the same 10-series sheets MU recoloured with a `c`.
profile_from: armour, not soft_armour. Vine, Silk and Wind are hide and cloth and took soft_armour; Spirit is plate. Its sheets are the Brass set's 10-series in the elf's green - upper_10c and lower_10c are upper_10_m and lower_10_m repainted, and the Brass set is plate_steel with brass ornaments - so the default plate_steel is what most of it is, and the `c` recolour changes the paint and not how the thing was made.

stats.note: The item's own row, copied from OpenMU's 0.75 initialiser rather than restated, with the call it came from beside it.
stats.from: openmu/src/Persistence/Initialization/Version075/Items/Armors.cs line 83. The 0.75 table, which is the version this server is being built to.
stats.call_note: ArmorInitializerBase.CreateArmor(number, slot, width, height, name, dropLevel, defense, durability, strengthRequirement, agilityRequirement, darkWizardClassLevel, darkKnightClassLevel, elfClassLevel). `armor.Group = (byte)(slot + 5)`, so slot 2 is group 7, 3 is 8 and 4 is 9.
stats.defense_note: Points of defence, in the row and summed into Player.ArmourDefense by Wear - see shared/Rows.cs.
stats.classes_from: The last three ints of the call are 0, 0, 1 - the Fairy Elf alone. Eighty agility beside forty strength is the row saying the same thing in stats.

sheet_from: Data/Player/upper_10c.OZJ (128x128), hide.jpg, skin_warrior_01.OZJ (256x256) and lower_09c.OZT (32x32), from MuMain. The .bmd names upper_10c.jpg, hide.jpg, skin_warrior_01.jpg and lower_09c.tga; 116 of the 182 triangles are on the first, 16 on hide, 46 on the skin and 4 on lower_09c.
sheet_note: upper_10c is a breastplate and backplate in dark green with gold ribbing and a gold scroll over the breast, and two shoulder plates below - the Brass Armor's upper_10_m repainted in the elf's green. Mean (78, 105, 92) at chroma 48. lower_09c is a curled green-and-gold fin on a 32-square whose alpha cuts 53% away, the ornament standing off the shoulders. skin_warrior_01 is the elf's own body sheet, which the piece carries for her bare arms. hide is MU capping the openings, a solid black square.
material_note: Seven islands and the Brass Armor's shape in green. Island 0 is 92 triangles - upper_10c's 76 and hide's 16, the cuirass and its caps - and islands 5 and 6 are 20 each, upper_10c's other 40, the shoulder plates: plate_steel. Islands 3 and 4 are 23 each, 46 together, skin_warrior_01's 46 exactly, at the same UV columns as the Vine Armor's arms: skin. Islands 1 and 2 are two triangles each, lower_09c's 4: the curled fins on crossed quads standing off the back, where the Brass Armor has its gold quills, and they take brass by the Brass set's own rule - a small ornament on its own .OZT is a cast piece, not a beaten plate, whatever colour it is painted. The green is dark - lower_10c averages lum about 60 - and a dark albedo at metallic 1.0 is the shape of the Bone set's fault, so it was weighed: here it is plate, as the Bronze-green Scale set's verdigris plate is (HelmMale07's note), and the gold ribbing is what the metal's highlight has to catch.
